chapter: George Lewis's first bands and instruments
title: Albert system clarinet and a Boehm-mixed instrument
summary: George says he always played Albert system, once tried Boehm, and had a clarinet his mother bought that mixed both.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: You always did play just Albert's system, I understand.
Did you ever try the Bain system? I tried.
Or bones and people? Yeah, it was a trial once, but I couldn't get it on with it.
Did you know anybody that played that when you were young or any time? No, I didn't know.

I never saw them until the 80 years. I wouldn't say they weren't playing, you know, but I never saw them until the 80 years. Because I get, somewhere or another I get confused. I was in some of those, yeah. But I did have, I had a crown that my mother had got me in the 20s, which was part Albert and part Bim. The bottom part was Bim with the top.
Oh yeah. Professor Minetta told us that some of the fellows used to use in that part. Yeah, my mother got it for me.

How was the tongue? The tongue was good, but one night I was working and it had a silver tube from the, right from where the valve begins coming down, the first half. Yeah. A whole silver tube in there. And all that ones had lost the tone. They just went down one night and I went to use it. And air was too hard, too many air with it. They just lost the tone. I brought it on Bimble between Dolphin and Bourbon. They had a violin maker there. And he was supposed to fix it and I didn't know if something went wrong. He died or something. He got away and I knew he'd get the crown. And it wasn't black. It was color of this, it was brownish.

Oh gosh. Do you think it was made that way, but somebody just got two different parts? The band and the... I don't know. It could have been two different parts. I can't imagine they'd make it ever that way, but probably somebody got two parts.
